clue.text: Boisterous tale gripping millions

indicators.note: something gripping another holds it inside, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: a tale is a story
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A rowdy yarn that holds millions of listeners spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: The M for millions goes inside the word for a tale, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather is wild and turbulent, and by extension a stormy person or meeting is boisterous and rough.

clue.text: Observer's weekly magazine?

blocks.note: first meaning: one who watches, a member of an audience
second meaning: The ..., a long-running British weekly political magazine

explanation.surface: Is this the Observer's weekly magazine supplement?
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, which makes the clue look like it is asking for its supplement; The Spectator is a rival British weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone who watches an event, an onlooker; The Spectator is also the name of a British weekly current-affairs title.

clue.text: Friendly Germans? Son and I kept moving

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so the letters before it get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Are the Germans friendly? My son and I kept travelling around.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on speaking terms is an idiom for being friendly enough with someone to talk to them.

clue.text: Expert following soldiers in danger

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the word for expert is placed second

blocks.note: soldiers are men in crossword shorthand
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist trailing behind troops who are in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat, something or someone that poses a danger.

clue.text: When copper should enter barriers in capital

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so these letters sit within the barriers

blocks.note: dams are barriers holding back water
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman ought to get past roadblocks in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer, but it is the metal, giving its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascus is the capital city of Syria.

clue.text: Cemetery in Durham town that needs no introduction

indicators.note: without an introduction the word loses its opening, so the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: Darlington is a market town in County Durham, north-east England

explanation.surface: A graveyard in a well-known town in County Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs no introduction' is the stock phrase for someone famous; here it literally removes the opening D.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia is the famous US military burial ground.

clue.text: Popped into a church in ancient city

indicators.note: popped suggests something burst open and scattered, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone nipped into a church while visiting an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popped into' reads as a phrase meaning visited, but 'Popped' acts on the word 'into' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was a major city of the ancient world, in what is now southern Turkey.

clue.text: Nothing in oven, confidence lost? So eat this!

definitions.text: Nothing in oven, confidence lost? So eat this!

indicators.note: letters that are lost have strayed from their places, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: No meal cooking and no faith in your kitchen skills? Then grab a ready meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay jumbles O with oven and confidence, and the full sentence describes when you would reach for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Convenience food is pre-prepared, ready-to-heat food for people who lack the time or skill to cook.

clue.text: Unwilling to go after son — that's laziness

indicators.note: going after means following behind, so the word for unwilling comes second

blocks.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
loth, also spelt loath, means reluctant

explanation.surface: A boy who won't follow on after his father is just being idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is one of the seven deadly sins, meaning idleness or a disinclination to work.

clue.text: Strong business partnership

blocks.note: first meaning: solid, sturdy
second meaning: a company, especially of partners such as lawyers

explanation.surface: A robust commercial alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm as an adjective means solid and steady; as a noun it is a business, classically a partnership of accountants or solicitors.

clue.text: Vital city on the Ruhr — one featured during most of talk

indicators.note: most of something is all but a little of it, so the final letter is dropped
something featured during an event appears in the middle of it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr valley
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A key German city gets a mention in most of the speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Talk loses its last letter to become TAL, then the I for one sits after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential and vital are synonyms, both meaning absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Dance beat — good one initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the words are kept

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
the first letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: The rhythm of a dance: a decent first attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: Beat looks like a musical noun but is the verb, as in giving someone a hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Argentina.

clue.text: Chance to meet him abroad in play

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so these letters are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An opportunity to encounter a man overseas in a theatre production.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceman Cometh is a 1939 stage play by the American dramatist Eugene O'Neill.

clue.text: Steal receipts

blocks.note: first meaning: to ... something that isn't yours
second meaning: the money ... in, as at a box office

explanation.walkthrough: Receipts suggests slips of paper from a till, but here it means takings.
explanation.definitionFit: To take can mean to steal, and the take is the amount of money received, as in a day's takings.

clue.text: Fine rain needs to stop — it's tricky on motorway

indicators.note: something tricky is twisted and devious, so the letters around it are rearranged

blocks.note: to scotch a plan is to put a stop to it
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
M is the prefix of British motorway numbers, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Drizzle ought to stop because driving on the motorway is treacherous.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch mist is a thick drizzle typical of the Scottish hills, a fine soaking rain.

clue.text: Singer his rector trained

indicators.note: trained means shaped or drilled into a new form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vocalist coached by the parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, especially a church choir, so a singer.

clue.text: Little boy wants to carry cuddly toy

blocks.note: Teddy is a pet name for Edward, a little boy's name
to bear is to carry

explanation.surface: A small lad wants to take his soft toy around with him.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is the classic stuffed toy bear given to children to cuddle.

clue.text: Get stranded in small car outside centre of Margate

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the central letter is taken
something outside another surrounds it, so the car word wraps round the letter

blocks.note: a runaround is a small car used for short trips
the middle letter of this seven-letter word; Margate is an English seaside town

explanation.surface: Getting stuck in a little car parked out in the middle of Margate.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that runs aground hits the bottom and is stuck there, stranded.

clue.text: Magnificent article written about a Spanish city

indicators.note: written about means wrapped round, so the first word surrounds the article

blocks.note: grand means magnificent
a is the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine piece of writing about a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The article A goes inside GRAND just before its D, and the clue's final 'a' is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, southern Spain, home of the Alhambra palace.

clue.text: Girl, one breaking object

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the numeral splits the other word

blocks.note: an end is an aim or object, as in 'to that end'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A girl, one of them, smashing something.
explanation.walkthrough: Object looks like a thing but means purpose here.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female given name, as in the children's author Enid Blyton.

clue.text: Small number, quiet at college feast

blocks.note: No. is the short form of number
sh is a call for quiet
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Only a few people, keeping hushed at a university banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh-up is British slang for a big, satisfying meal; nosh means food.

clue.text: Poor audition cost me the lead in Yorkshire TV series noted for its humour

definitions.text: TV series noted for its humour

indicators.note: a poor performance is badly put together, so these letters come out in the wrong order
the lead is what goes in front, so only the opening letter of the county is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of this northern English county

explanation.surface: A bad tryout lost me the starring part in a funny programme made by Yorkshire Television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lead in Yorkshire TV series' reads as a starring role; Yorkshire Television was a real ITV company, but only its Y is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy, or sitcom, is a television series built around recurring characters in comic situations.

clue.text: Pass out with onset of muzziness and cramp

indicators.note: out here means disordered or out of place, so the letters are rearranged
the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Fainting as you start feeling dizzy, then getting a muscle cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass out' looks like a phrasal verb meaning faint, but 'out' acts on 'Pass' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary muscle contraction, which is what a cramp is.

clue.text: A secluded place for lovemaking? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word stops before its final letter

blocks.note: nooky is informal British slang for sex

explanation.surface: Somewhere private for a romantic tryst? Almost.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or recess, a quiet secluded spot.

clue.text: Vessel seen in China or Taiwan

indicators.note: seen in means visible inside, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A ship spotted in Chinese or Taiwanese waters.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a ship near Asian ports, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the body's main artery, the largest blood vessel, leaving the heart.

clue.text: Temptingly tasty? Very — those cooked with hint of mustard added in

indicators.note: a hint is only a trace, so just the first letter of the condiment is used
cooked means altered by preparation, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: too means very, as in 'too kind'
taken as written
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: Delicious? Extremely, once those are cooked with a dab of mustard stirred in.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome describes food that is appetising and delicious, good enough to get your teeth into.

clue.text: Crowd at ancient city in overwhelming defeat

blocks.note: a mass is a crowd of people
Acre is an ancient port city in present-day Israel, famous from the Crusades

explanation.surface: A throng at an old city suffering a crushing military loss.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport and war, a massacre is informally a one-sided rout, a crushing defeat.

clue.text: Eight-legged creature? And the rest!

blocks.note: first meaning: the arachnid
second meaning: a raised cue rest used in snooker and billiards

explanation.surface: An arachnid? And all the others too!
explanation.walkthrough: 'And the rest' reads as 'et cetera', but it is a snooker rest; a spider is the cue rest with raised legs for playing over another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is an eight-legged arachnid, and also the name of a cue rest with legs used in snooker.
